notes: `skeleton` is the command with every LOLBAS placeholder ({REMOTEURL}, {PATH}, ...) and every path/URL-shaped token removed, leaving the tokens an operator cannot change while still performing the documented abuse.
Commands whose skeleton is empty are dropped: with no invariant token there is nothing to confirm, and a match on the binary name alone is already what core/data/lolbas_binaries.json reports.
Separate from lolbas_binaries.json on purpose — the Layer 2 lookup and the process module are unaffected by this file.

wsb.exe.usecase: Fileless execution of arbitrary commands in an EDR-free environment, with access to files on the host system, while the host-side process tree is masked by the Sandbox client binaries.
wsb.exe.description: Allows the specified folder to be accessible from within the Windows Sandbox, mounted under `C:\users\WDAGUtilityAccount\Desktop` with the same folder name as the source folder. This allows, for example, for copying payloads from the host system into the sandbox (seen here), copying payloads from the sandbox back to the host system, or for accessing arbitrary host system files by the sandbox.

wsb.exe.command:
wsb start
wsb share --id YOUR_ID -f {PATH_ABSOLUTE:folder} -s c:\SOME_FOLDER --allow-write
wsb exec -r System --id YOUR_ID -c "cmd.exe /c copy {PATH_ABSOLUTE} c:\SOME_FOLDER"

wscript.exe.usecase: Execute hidden code to evade defensive counter measures
wscript.exe.description: Execute script stored in an alternate data stream

wsl.exe.usecase: Performs execution of arbitrary Linux commands as root without need for password.
Performs execution of arbitrary Linux commands.
wsl.exe.description: Executes Linux command (for example via bash) as the default user (unless stated otherwise using `-u <username>`) on the default WSL distro (unless stated otherwise using `-d <distro name>`)

wuauclt.exe.description: Loads and executes DLL code on attach.

xbootmgr.exe.usecase: Executes code as part of post-trace automation flow.
xbootmgr.exe.description: Executes an executable after the trace is complete using the callBack parameter.

xbootmgr.exe.usecase: Executes code as part of pre-trace automation or staging.
xbootmgr.exe.description: Executes an executable before each trace run using the preTraceCmd parameter.

xwizard.exe.usecase: Run a com object created in registry to evade defensive counter measures
xwizard.exe.description: Xwizard.exe running a custom class that has been added to the registry. The /t and /u switch prevent an error message in later Windows 10 builds.
